mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 50% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4% signals labor market weakness, which may lead to economic downturn and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time when UNRATE exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high and the federal funds rate is rising, it indicates monetary tightening, which can lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time when both CPIAUCSL > 250 and FEDFUNDS > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates reduced economic activity, which may lead to negative equity returns, especially in the late stages of the business cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time when GDPC1 growth slows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with positive equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time when PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 indicates a weakening housing market, which may lead to broader economic slowdown and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time when HOUST < 1200.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals economic contraction, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time when INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in retail sales (RSAFS) after an economic shock indicates recovery, which may boost equity markets.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 30% of the time when RSAFS growth is strong.
